topics.label: Course Welcome, Objectives, and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and frames the course for students of diverse disciplines.

topics.label: Biological Foundations and Experimental Models of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how cancer arises through accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal tissue differentiation and architecture, as well as the experimental methods used to model these processes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Histology of Tumor Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the histological and physical characteristics that distinguish benign growth from invasive and metastatic malignancy, using tissue examples such as colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Tumor Classification, Nomenclature, and Pathophysiological Effects
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the naming conventions for neoplasms and explain the direct physiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant tumors cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer Epidemiology Across Human Tissues and Animal Species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare the incidence, prevalence, and mortality patterns of various cancers across human organ systems and throughout the animal kingdom.

topics.label: Clinical Principles and Modalities of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the rationale, effectiveness, and limitations of population screening methods for detecting pre-malignant lesions across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Practical Information
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reiterating the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping information for upcoming sessions.
